title: Trendline Break
teaches: The trendline break as we trade it: a leader above its 200-day drifts tight under a falling line drawn over the daily highs, the buy is the trade through the line and the prior day's high at market in regular hours and never more than 4% past the line, the stop sits a few cents under the trigger day's low, a close back under the line is a warning and not an exit, a third comes off at 3R and 5R with the rest on the trail, and a break on its own is a warning, not a reversal.

facts.quote: A downtrend line has a negative slope formed by connecting two or more high points.

questions.q: A falling trendline for a breakout is drawn over what?
choices: The daily highs, wicks included
The daily closes, not the wicks
The daily lows
The 50-day moving average line
questions.why: The daily highs, wicks included. A downtrend line connects high points, drawn above the peaks and not through price.
questions.lesson_line: Draw it over the highs, wicks and all. Start at the pullback's highest high.

wrong.The daily closes, not the wicks: A line over the closes cuts through the wicks. The line goes over the highs.
wrong.The daily lows: Lows make a rising line under price. The falling line sits over the highs.
wrong.The 50-day moving average line: An average is not a trendline. The line is drawn on the highs themselves.

questions.q: On its own, a trendline break is a warning, not a reversal.
questions.why: True. A break is merely a warning that a change in trend may be imminent. The Insider calls it a heads-up, not a trading signal.
questions.lesson_line: A broken line is a heads-up. It is not a reversal by itself.

questions.q: Where does the stop go on a trendline break bought during the day?
choices: A few cents under the day's low
Exactly on the falling line itself
Under the 200-day average line
questions.answer: A few cents under the day's low
questions.why: A few cents under the trigger day's low, as it stands at entry. Not exactly on it, and not on the line.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the trigger day's low.

wrong.Exactly on the falling line itself: The line is the trigger, not the stop. A close back under it is a warning; the stop is the exit.
wrong.Under the 200-day average line: That is far below the trade. The stop sits close, near the trigger day's low.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: We do not buy a trendline break in a stock under its ___-day average.
questions.why: 200. The trigger day closes above the 200-day. No longs below the 200-day, unless it is a parabolic long.
questions.lesson_line: Above the 200-day first. Then look at the line.

questions.q: We buy trendline breaks in leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in a strong group.
questions.why: True. Buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups.
questions.lesson_line: A clean line in a laggard is still a laggard. Buy the leaders.

questions.q: A trendline break is a good spot to add to a position you already hold.
questions.why: False. A break is a first entry, never an add. Full size once, one stop.
questions.lesson_line: Full size once, one stop. A break is an entry, not an add.

questions.q: The stop sits with the broker as a real order, and it only moves up.
questions.why: True. A real stop order with the broker, not a stop kept in your head. It only moves up, never down or wider.
questions.lesson_line: A real order with the broker, moved up only.

questions.q: Which event is the buy on a trendline break?
choices: Trades through line and prior high
Price just touches the line from below
A close 3% past the line
The 50-day crossing the 200-day
questions.answer: Trades through line and prior high
questions.why: It trades through the line and the prior day's high, during regular hours, bought at market. That is our default trigger.
questions.lesson_line: Through the line and the prior high, in hours, at market.

wrong.Price just touches the line from below: Touching the line is not a break. Price has to trade through it.
wrong.A close 3% past the line: Our default does not wait for a close 3% past the line. That filter is for long-term lines.
wrong.The 50-day crossing the 200-day: A crossing of averages is a different signal. The trigger is the line and the prior high.

questions.q: We wait for a close 3% past the line before we buy.
questions.why: False. Do not wait for a close 3% past the line. That filter is for long-term lines and would use up most of the 4% chase limit.
questions.lesson_line: No 3% filter. Waiting costs most of the chase limit.

questions.q: Two highs fix a falling line. How far apart should they be?
choices: At least 5 sessions
Any two days
At least 1 session
At least 3 sessions
questions.why: At least 5 sessions. Touches too close together may be nothing more than noise, so our working rule is anchors at least 5 sessions apart.
questions.lesson_line: Space the anchors out. Two highs a few days apart prove nothing.

wrong.Any two days: Points too close together make noise, not a line.
wrong.At least 1 session: One session apart is far too close. Our rule needs at least 5.
wrong.At least 3 sessions: Three is still too close for our rule, which needs at least 5.

questions.q: A wick through the line before the trigger day cancels the first break.
questions.why: False. A first break means no daily close above the line before the trigger day. A wick through is allowed.
questions.lesson_line: Closes count, wicks do not. No close above the line before the trigger.

questions.q: We take trendline breaks only in stocks at $10 or more that trade $20 million a day.
questions.why: True. Price $10 or more and at least $20 million traded a day.
questions.lesson_line: A clean line in a thin stock is still a thin stock.

questions.q: How far over its 10-day average is too far to buy a break?
choices: More than 10%
More than 25%
More than 5%
More than 2%
questions.why: More than 10% over the 10-day average. Skip a long that stretched.
questions.lesson_line: Stretched is a pass. More than 10% over the 10-day, skip it.

wrong.More than 25%: A long that far over its average is long gone. The line is 10%.

questions.q: It helps when the index itself is breaking its own downtrend line.
questions.why: True. The index breaking its own downtrend line or making a wedge pop is a cue. Kell: as the index pops, the strongest stocks break out.
questions.lesson_line: Best when the market breaks its own line too.

questions.q: Which market reading allows a full-size trendline break?
choices: Green
Yellow
Orange
Red
questions.why: Green: full size. Yellow is smaller and fewer, Orange is A+ only, and Red is mostly cash.
questions.lesson_line: Green is full size. Every other color cuts it down.

wrong.Yellow: Yellow is smaller and fewer, not full size.
wrong.Red: Red is mostly cash and shorts.

questions.q: Bought at 26.97 with the stop at 26.73. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 27.69. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. MSFT got there the next day.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: The line's value is 50.00. What is the most we pay?
questions.why: 52.00. We never buy more than 4% above the buy point, and here the buy point is the line.
questions.lesson_line: Four percent over the line is the limit. Chasing costs size.

questions.q: After entry, a close back under the line means sell at once.
questions.why: False. A close back under the line is a warning, not an exit. The stop is the exit and only moves up.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the line is a warning. The stop is the exit.

questions.q: Which lead-in to the line is best?
choices: Tight drift down, volume drying up
Lows rising into the line, volume fading
Wide swings under the line
One big drop into the line
questions.answer: Tight drift down, volume drying up
questions.why: A tight drift down. The closes sit close under the line and the daily ranges shrink.
questions.lesson_line: Tight and quiet under the line. Not rising into it.

wrong.Lows rising into the line, volume fading: That is wedging up into the line, not the tight drift down this setup wants.
wrong.Wide swings under the line: Wide swings are not tight. The average daily range should shrink.
wrong.One big drop into the line: A big drop makes a steep line. The steeper the line, the less valid it is.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: A fast mover's last third trails on a close under the ___-day.
questions.why: 10. The 10-day for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one. Sell on a close below it.
questions.lesson_line: Trail the rising average. Sell the close below it, not the touch.

questions.q: Into a vertical climax burst, we sell a big part of the position.
questions.why: True. A climax burst on the way up is for selling into. It is a judgment call, and selling a big part is the rule.
questions.lesson_line: A burst up is for selling into. Take the money.

questions.q: A stock sits under falling 10 and 21-day averages that act as resistance. A line break there is?
choices: Not this setup
A strong buy
Fine if volume is big
questions.why: Not this setup. A stock under falling averages acting as resistance is out. Kell: avoid a downtrend when the averages act as resistance.
questions.lesson_line: Falling averages overhead are supply. Wait for a leader.

wrong.A strong buy: Falling averages above price are supply, not support.
wrong.Fine if volume is big: Volume does not fix a stock under falling averages.

questions.q: If the highs do not line up, we draw the line through the closest points anyway.
questions.why: False. It is best not to force the issue. A proper trendline should never be forced.
questions.lesson_line: No line, no trade. Never force a line through the points.

questions.q: Bought at 109.23 with the stop at 106.79. How far below the buy is the stop, in percent?
questions.why: 2.23%. The buy minus the stop, divided by the buy. That is inside the 3% a stop usually sits within.
questions.lesson_line: Buy minus stop, over the buy. Know the distance before you size.

questions.q: Buy the open?
questions.story: The falling line sits at 50.00 today. News gaps the stock open to 52.40.
choices: Pass; 4.8% over the line
Buy at market; it has momentum
Buy half size
questions.why: Pass. A gap open more than 4% above the line is no trade; this one is 4.8% over. Chasing costs size, because the stop stays put.
questions.lesson_line: More than 4% over the line is no trade. Let it go.

wrong.Buy at market; it has momentum: Over the 4% cap, the stop stays far away and the shares shrink. That is a chase.
wrong.Buy half size: Half of a chase is still a chase. The line is 4%.

questions.q: Buy the next break?
questions.story: Your break was stopped on Monday. On Wednesday the stock makes a new high, and you redraw the line through it.
choices: No; a redrawn line is no trigger
Yes; the new line is cleaner
Yes, with a tighter stop
questions.answer: No; a redrawn line is no trigger
questions.why: No. After a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger. Do not redraw the same line to get back in.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out is not a reason to redraw the line.

wrong.Yes; the new line is cleaner: Redrawing the line to get back in is the named mistake.
wrong.Yes, with a tighter stop: Tightening the stop does not make a redrawn line a trigger.

questions.q: Is this our trendline break?
questions.story: A stock 20% under its 200-day breaks a 60-session falling line on twice its usual volume.
choices: No; it is under the 200-day
Yes; the volume is big
Yes, if the line is long
questions.why: No. The trigger day must close above the 200-day, and we do not buy longs below it. A long line and big volume do not change that.
questions.lesson_line: The 200-day comes first. A beaten-down stock is not our break.

wrong.Yes; the volume is big: Big volume does not lift a stock over its 200-day.
wrong.Yes, if the line is long: A long line does not change the 200-day rule.

questions.q: Trendline break or flat top?
questions.story: Three highs sit at exactly 50.00 over six weeks. You are weighing a buy through 50.00.
choices: A flat-top break, not this setup
A trendline break
A wedge pop
questions.answer: A flat-top break, not this setup
questions.why: A flat top. A trendline falls, at least a little, from lower swing highs. A line with no slope is a horizontal resistance break.
questions.lesson_line: No slope, no trendline. Three equal highs are a flat top.

wrong.A trendline break: The highs are level, so there is no falling line to break.
wrong.A wedge pop: A wedge pop follows a decline and reclaims the fast averages. Level highs do not.

questions.q: Bought at 26.97, stop 26.73. The stock trades to 28.17. How many R is that?
questions.why: 5R. Each R is the fill minus the stop. That is where the second third comes off.
questions.lesson_line: Count in R, not dollars. 5R is the second trim.

questions.q: The stop moves to breakeven somewhere between 2R and 5R.
questions.why: True. Stop to breakeven at 2R to 5R, at the first trim by default.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim.

questions.q: What does the index break do for your list?
questions.story: The S&P 500 breaks its own downtrend line on a strong day. Your list holds three valid line breaks.
choices: It helps; leaders break with it
Nothing; indexes do not matter
Skip them; the move is already late
questions.answer: It helps; leaders break with it
questions.why: It helps. The index breaking its own downtrend line is a cue, and Kell says the strongest stocks break out as the index pops.
questions.lesson_line: A market that breaks its own line lifts the leaders.

wrong.Nothing; indexes do not matter: The market reading is a guide for every setup, and the index break is a cue for this one.
wrong.Skip them; the move is already late: The cue says the strongest stocks break out as the index does. It is a reason to look.

questions.q: Where is the first overhead supply for a falling-line break?
choices: The old high where the line starts
The 200-day average below the line
Yesterday's low under the line
The lowest low under the line
questions.answer: The old high where the line starts
questions.why: The old high where the line starts. Price reached it 77% of the time in Bulkowski's study, so expect a fight there.
questions.lesson_line: The anchor high is overhead. Know where it is before you buy.

wrong.The 200-day average below the line: The 200-day is below a stock that qualifies. Supply sits above.
wrong.Yesterday's low under the line: That is where the stop sits, not supply.
wrong.The lowest low under the line: That low is below the line. Supply sits above, at the old high.

questions.q: Which is the setup, and which is the trigger?
questions.story: A stock jumps 25% in 20 sessions, then drifts for 8 sessions under a falling line of two highs.
choices: Flag is the setup, line the trigger
Line is the setup; flag is the context
Two setups, so two separate trades
questions.answer: Flag is the setup, line the trigger
questions.why: The flag is the setup and the line is its trigger. A trendline break needs no pole, only a line of lower swing highs.
questions.lesson_line: The flag is the setup. The line is how you get in.

wrong.Line is the setup; flag is the context: When the line is the top of a flag, the flag is the setup and the line is its trigger.
wrong.Two setups, so two separate trades: One structure, one trade, one stop. A break is never an add.

questions.q: Trendline break or wedge pop?
questions.story: A stock closed 12 of the last 15 sessions under its 20 EMA. A bar then clears a tight range and both fast averages.
choices: A wedge pop; averages reclaimed
A trendline break of a long line
A flat-top break at a ceiling
questions.why: A wedge pop. It follows a decline with at least 8 of the last 15 closes under the 20 EMA. Then it reclaims the 10 and 20 EMAs. A trendline break already holds the fast averages.
questions.lesson_line: Lost the averages, then reclaimed them: that is the pop.

wrong.A trendline break of a long line: A trendline break has the fast averages already reclaimed or held on the trigger day. This stock lost them.
wrong.A flat-top break at a ceiling: Nothing here is a level ceiling. The tell is the lost and reclaimed averages.

questions.q: Take it?
questions.story: The reading is Orange. A valid break has a stop 6% away, and a key level sits just above.
choices: No; a B- is a pass in Orange
Yes; the line is valid
Yes, at half size
questions.answer: No; a B- is a pass in Orange
questions.why: No. Orange takes A+ setups only. A 6% stop and a key level just above grade this one B- or lower, so it is a pass.
questions.lesson_line: In an Orange market, only the best setups get through.

wrong.Yes; the line is valid: A valid line is not enough in Orange. It has to grade A+.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not turn a B- into an A+. Orange takes A+ only.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: The honest stop sits 4.5% under the buy. Your usual size would risk too much.
choices: Take the smaller size, or skip
Tighten the stop to 3% to fit
Use full size and accept the risk
questions.answer: Take the smaller size, or skip
questions.why: Take the smaller size the formula gives, or skip. Never tighten the stop to fit.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sets the size. Never back-fit a tighter stop.

wrong.Tighten the stop to 3% to fit: Tightening the honest stop to fit the size is the mistake. The size moves, not the stop.
wrong.Use full size and accept the risk: Full size on a wide stop risks more than the rule allows.

questions.q: What was the weak spot?
questions.story: A break barely clears the line, closing 0.4% over it on thin volume. You buy it. Next day it closes back under the line.
choices: A thin break barely over the line
The stop was too tight for the line
Nothing; breaks just fail
questions.answer: A thin break barely over the line
questions.why: A thin break that barely cleared the line. A break with volume matters more than one without, and this kind often closes back under.
questions.lesson_line: A barely-there break on thin volume is a weak break.

wrong.The stop was too tight for the line: The stop followed the rule. The weakness was the break itself.
wrong.Nothing; breaks just fail: Some do, but this one showed its weakness on the day: thin volume and a close barely over the line.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You bought a break 10 trading days ago. It sits at 0.6R after three flat closes with no higher high.
choices: Sell; under 1R after 10 days
Hold; the stop has not traded
Add; it is cheap
questions.why: Sell. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold. No follow-through within a few sessions is itself the signal.
questions.lesson_line: No follow-through is the signal. Free the money.

wrong.Hold; the stop has not traded: The time stop is its own exit. Under 1R after 10 days, the money goes elsewhere.
wrong.Add; it is cheap: A break is never an add. And no follow-through is a weak sign.

questions.q: Take the break?
questions.story: Lows rise into the falling line for three weeks, and volume fades each day. Today it pokes through.
choices: No; it is wedging up into the line
Yes; it broke the line on the day
Yes, if volume picks up on the break
questions.answer: No; it is wedging up into the line
questions.why: No. Rising lows into the line on shrinking volume is not the tight drift down this setup wants.
questions.lesson_line: Wedging up into the line is not a tight drift down.

wrong.Yes; it broke the line on the day: Breaking the line is not enough. The shape into it has to be a tight drift down.
wrong.Yes, if volume picks up on the break: The wedge up into the line is the problem, and volume on the day does not fix the shape.

questions.q: A break gives no price target. What takes its place?
choices: Trims at 3R and 5R, then a trail
The height of the pullback
The old high, all out
questions.answer: Trims at 3R and 5R, then a trail
questions.why: Trims at 3R and 5R, then a trail. Brandt: a trendline violation does not carry with it a price target.
questions.lesson_line: No target from the pattern. The R-based trims do the job.

wrong.The height of the pullback: A measuring rule is not ours. The trims are set in R.
wrong.The old high, all out: The old high is overhead supply, not a target. We trim in thirds and trail the rest.

questions.q: Account 50,000. Risk 0.5%. Buy 109.23, stop 106.79. How many shares?
questions.why: 102. Account times risk percent, divided by the buy minus the stop, rounded down. The stop sets the size, and the position stays under the 40% cap.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: You hold the last third of a fast mover after both trims. Today it closes under its 10-day.
choices: Sell the last third on that close
Hold until the 50-day breaks
Move the stop down
questions.answer: Sell the last third on that close
questions.why: Sell the last third. A fast mover trails the 10-day, and we sell on a close below it.
questions.lesson_line: The trail is a close under the 10-day. Sell it.

wrong.Hold until the 50-day breaks: The trail is the 10-day for a fast mover, not the 50-day.
wrong.Move the stop down: The stop only moves up, never down or wider.

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: You bought at 40.00 with the stop at 39.00. It gaps open at 38.20, and the first 30-minute low is 37.80.
choices: Out; the loss is past 2R
The new stop is 37.80
Hold; gaps fill
questions.why: Out. On a gap through the stop the first 30-minute low is the new stop, but past 2R you get out. A low of 37.80 is more than 2R from 40.00.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop has a ceiling of 2R.

wrong.The new stop is 37.80: The 30-minute low is the stop only while the loss is inside 2R. This one is past it.
wrong.Hold; gaps fill: Hope is not a rule. The gap rule has a ceiling, and this is past it.

questions.q: On one stock we take at most 3 tries a week and 6 a month.
questions.why: True. After a stop-out, only a new trigger buys it again. The cap is 3 tries a week and 6 a month on one stock.
questions.lesson_line: Three tries a week, six a month. Then leave it alone.

questions.q: Buy it?
questions.story: A clean break sets up for tomorrow. The company reports after the close in 2 days.
choices: No; the report is inside 3 days
Yes; the line is clean and tight
Yes, and sell before the report
questions.answer: No; the report is inside 3 days
questions.why: No. No new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report. Hold through one only if the trade is up 5R.
questions.lesson_line: Stay three days clear of the report, or wait.

wrong.Yes; the line is clean and tight: A clean line does not move the earnings window.
wrong.Yes, and sell before the report: The rule is no new buy in that window, not a quick trade through it.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You are up 4R in four days on a vertical, wide-range burst.
choices: Sell a big part into the burst
Add; it is going parabolic
Hold it all; the trail will handle it
questions.answer: Sell a big part into the burst
questions.why: Sell a big part into it. A climax run on your own long is for selling into; how much is a judgment call.
questions.lesson_line: A vertical burst is for selling into.

wrong.Add; it is going parabolic: A break is never an add, and a burst is for selling into.
wrong.Hold it all; the trail will handle it: The trail catches the turn late. A burst is the moment to bank a big part.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You bought at 30.00 with the stop at 29.00. It trades to 33.00.
choices: Sell a third; stop to breakeven
Sell half now and trail the rest
Hold all of it until 5R
questions.answer: Sell a third; stop to breakeven
questions.why: Sell a third at 3R and move the stop to breakeven, 30.00. The next third waits for 5R.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, then the stop to breakeven.

wrong.Sell half now and trail the rest: The rule is a third at 3R and a third at 5R, not half at once.
wrong.Hold all of it until 5R: Holding it all risks a 3R gain for a scratch. The first third comes off at 3R.

questions.q: You followed every rule. What was the loss?
questions.story: You bought through an 83-session line at 18.79 with the stop at 18.53. The break closed only 0.39% over the line. Next day the low was 18.39.
choices: A planned loss; the stop did its job
A mistake; the stop was too tight
A reason to redraw the line
questions.answer: A planned loss; the stop did its job
questions.why: A planned loss. The stop is the exit and it did its job. A break that barely clears the line is a weak one.
questions.lesson_line: A stop that trades is the plan working.

wrong.A mistake; the stop was too tight: The stop sits a few cents under the day's low by the rule. Widening it to dodge a loss is the mistake.
wrong.A reason to redraw the line: Redrawing the line to get back in is the named mistake. Only a new trigger buys again.

questions.q: What do you do at the open?
questions.story: You bought at 145.75 with the stop at 144.17, so 3R is 150.49. The next session opens at 152.00.
choices: Sell a third at the open
Hold; wait for the close
Sell it all
questions.answer: Sell a third at the open
questions.why: Sell a third at the open. A trim level the day opens past is taken at the open. The stock then fell to 144.06 and the stop traded, but the trim had banked a gain.
questions.lesson_line: Take the trim the open hands you.

wrong.Hold; wait for the close: The level is already passed. Waiting gave the gap time to fill.
wrong.Sell it all: A third at 3R. The rest waits for 5R and the trail.

questions.q: Where is the buy?
questions.story: A stock doubles in a few weeks, then forms a tight, shallow flag. A falling line crosses the flag's highs.
choices: Over the pattern's highest high
Through the falling line at once
At the 50-day average
questions.why: Over the pattern's highest high. The flag's trendline break fails too often on a high tight flag, so buy the pattern's highest high instead.
questions.lesson_line: On a high tight flag, buy the pattern high, not the line.

wrong.Through the falling line at once: On a high tight flag the flag's trendline break fails too often. That is the named mistake.
wrong.At the 50-day average: A doubled stock holds far above its 50-day. The buy is on strength, over the high.

questions.q: You were stopped out. What now?
questions.story: You bought at 200.06 with the stop at 197.41. The low was 197.22, 19 cents under the stop. It closed 209.53 and reached 217 within a week.
choices: Only a new trigger re-enters
Buy it back at once; it ran 6%
Move your next stop lower
questions.why: Only a new trigger. After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade with its own stop and every rule.
questions.lesson_line: It ran without you. Only a new trigger buys it back.

wrong.Buy it back at once; it ran 6%: Chasing what ran is the mistake. A re-entry needs a new trigger.
wrong.Move your next stop lower: The stop is a few cents under the day's low. Moving it lower to avoid a stop-out is not the rule.

questions.q: What does the quiet volume say?
questions.story: A clean line of 3 touches over 85 sessions breaks, but on only 0.86x the 50-day average volume.
choices: Weak; a break with volume matters more
Nothing; volume is noise
Strong; no one is selling
questions.answer: Weak; a break with volume matters more
questions.why: Weak. A trendline break with volume matters more than a break without. This quiet one is a poor sign.
questions.lesson_line: Volume confirms the break. A quiet break is a weak one.

wrong.Nothing; volume is noise: The Insider says a break with volume matters more than one without.
wrong.Strong; no one is selling: Quiet volume on a break is not strength. Buyers did not show up.

questions.q: Take the break?
questions.story: A steep three-week drop leaves two lower highs. A line through them breaks today.
choices: Pass; steep line, two close highs
Take it; the line broke on the day
Take it, but on half the size
questions.answer: Pass; steep line, two close highs
questions.why: Pass. Buying breaks of steep lines is a named mistake, and two highs this close may be nothing more than noise.
questions.lesson_line: A steep plunge draws a steep line. Skip it.

wrong.Take it; the line broke on the day: The steeper the line, the less valid it is. A break of it is not enough.
wrong.Take it, but on half the size: Size does not repair a steep line with two close highs.

questions.q: The stop traded. Did the rules fail?
questions.story: You buy a clean break at 48.12 with the stop at 47.25. The next session is the first day of a market break, and the stop trades.
choices: No; a planned loss, rules kept
Yes; we should have waited a day
Yes; the stop was too wide
questions.answer: No; a planned loss, rules kept
questions.why: No. The stop is the exit and it did its job. The next session was the first day of the February 2020 market break, so the loss was the planned 1.80%.
questions.lesson_line: A valid break can lose. The stop makes it small.

wrong.Yes; we should have waited a day: Waiting would have been a different trade. The loss here was the planned 1.80%.
wrong.Yes; the stop was too wide: The stop was 1.80% away, inside the 3% a stop usually sits within.

questions.q: In our test with a fixed stop and no trims, 78.8% of triggers were eventually stopped. What does that show?
choices: Trims and a trail bank the gains
The line is a bad signal
Wider stops would win more
questions.answer: Trims and a trail bank the gains
questions.why: Trims and a trail bank the gains. A fixed stop without trims gives winners back: 78.8% were eventually stopped. We sell a third at 3R and 5R and trail the rest.
questions.lesson_line: Bank a third at 3R and 5R. Trail the rest.

wrong.The line is a bad signal: Many reached 3R first. The exits, not the entry, gave the gains back.
wrong.Wider stops would win more: A wider stop means fewer shares, not more winners.

questions.q: Write the plan.
questions.story: MSFT, January 2012: a mega-cap drifts tight under a five-month falling line, then trades through it.
choices: Buy 26.97, stop 26.73, a third at 3R
Buy 26.97, stop 25.00, hold it all
Wait for a close 3% past the line
questions.why: Buy at market, 26.97. Stop a few cents under the day's low, 26.73. A third comes off at 3R. MSFT got there the next day.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop, trim, trail. Write it before the open.

wrong.Buy 26.97, stop 25.00, hold it all: The stop belongs a few cents under the day's low, 26.73. And a third comes off at 3R.
wrong.Wait for a close 3% past the line: Our default trigger is the trade through the line, not a close 3% past it.

questions.q: Which gets the bigger size?
questions.story: Two valid breaks. A: a leader tight under the line, room overhead, Green market. B: Yellow market, the stop 4% away, a key level just above.
choices: A; every cue lines up
B; it has the wider stop
Equal; the line is the same
questions.why: A. Tight under the line on drying volume, room to the first anchor high and a Green market is the A+ end. A Yellow market (smaller and fewer), a 4% stop and a key level just above grade it lower.
questions.lesson_line: Same line, different grade. The spot and the market set the size.

wrong.B; it has the wider stop: A wider stop grades it down, and so does the key level just above.
wrong.Equal; the line is the same: The line is the same, but the market, the stop and the room are not.

questions.q: Is this the first break?
questions.story: Two weeks ago a stock closed over its falling line, then slid back under. Today it trades through the line again.
choices: No; it already closed through
Yes; a wick is allowed
Yes; it is a fresh day
questions.why: No. A first break has no daily close above the line before the trigger day. A close two weeks ago means this is not the first.
questions.lesson_line: One close over the line spends the first break.

wrong.Yes; a wick is allowed: A wick is allowed, but a close above the line is not. This one closed over it.
wrong.Yes; it is a fresh day: The rule counts closes above the line since the first anchor, not days.

questions.q: Price reached the start of the line 77% of the time, so we sell all at that old high.
questions.why: False. The old high is overhead supply, context and not a rule. No pattern target replaces the R-based trims.
questions.lesson_line: The old high is supply to respect, not a target.

questions.q: Take the break?
questions.story: A clean break of a long line in a stock with an RS rating of 55, in a lagging group.
choices: No; the stock is not a leader
Yes; the line is clean
Yes, with a smaller stop and size
questions.answer: No; the stock is not a leader
questions.why: No. We buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups. A clean line in a laggard is still a laggard.
questions.lesson_line: The stock comes before the line.

wrong.Yes; the line is clean: A clean line is only one of the gates. The RS rating is another.
wrong.Yes, with a smaller stop and size: A smaller stop does not make a laggard a leader.

questions.q: Hidden ticker. A pullback drifts tight under a falling line. Above its 200-day? Take the break or pass.
choices: Take it; above 200-day, tight drift
Pass; the stock is under the 200-day
Pass; the line is really a flat top
questions.why: Take it. The close sits above the 200-day and the pullback drifts tight under a shallow line. The break ran straight to new highs.
questions.lesson_line: The 200-day and the tight drift first. Then the line.

wrong.Pass; the stock is under the 200-day: Look again: price sits above the 200-day here.
wrong.Pass; the line is really a flat top: The line falls, slowly. A slow slope is still a slope.

questions.q: Hidden ticker. A good-looking falling line. Is the stock above its 200-day? Take the break or pass.
choices: Pass; it is under the 200-day
Take it; the line is long
Take it; the volume is fine
questions.why: Pass. On the trigger day the close was 4.9% under the 200-day, so the line does not matter. A good-looking line under a flat 200-day is not our break.
questions.lesson_line: A fine line under the 200-day is still a pass.

wrong.Take it; the line is long: A long line is only one gate. The 200-day is another.
wrong.Take it; the volume is fine: Fine volume does not lift a stock over its 200-day.

questions.q: Which one do we take?
questions.story: Four breaks today. A: under its 200-day. B: reports in 2 days. C: a leader, tight under the line. D: gaps 5% over the line.
choices: A; the line is the longest
B; the volume is biggest
C; a leader tight under the line
D; it has momentum
questions.answer: C; a leader tight under the line
questions.why: C. A stock under the 200-day, a report inside 3 days and a gap over 4% each rule one out. C is the leader that is tight under the line.
questions.lesson_line: Run every gate. One failure ends it.

wrong.A; the line is the longest: It is under the 200-day. A long line does not fix that.
wrong.B; the volume is biggest: A report inside 3 days ends it. Big volume does not move the window.
wrong.D; it has momentum: A gap more than 4% over the line is no trade.

Leadership: the card's gate is RS 80 or more (settled); its grading rows quote RS 90 or more for A+ and 'RS under 80' for B-. q05 and q60 key the gate; the 90 is never keyed.

Stop width: the card's settled tl.stop_width (about 3%; smaller size or skip; never tighten) is keyed in q36. His statistics (the 77% to the start of the line, used in q32 and q59 as context only) are from bull markets and best-case exits. Brandt's page is futures-first and an experience figure, not a study.

The support rule: ChartSchool and the Insider are both StockCharts but different publications; CMT, Bulkowski, Brandt and TraderLion are separate publishers. Every rule key carries house: true on the card, the rulebook or the dossier, with the web quotes agreeing. The dossier's example numbers (d1) were read off our own daily bars by the research scan (dossier sections 12 and 13), not from a public page; the owner has not picked his ten. The walk-throughs (NUE, MSFT, SCHW) and the real cases (BHC, MCK, CAT, EL, DHR, LBTYA, GOOGL, DIS) depend on them. The fills are the scan's: the higher of the line and the prior day's high, or the open on a gap, with the stop five cents under the trigger day's low; a live market order fills a little differently. Prices are split-adjusted, and HLF passes the $10 rule only in adjusted prices (not used here).

The chart questions (q61 MCK asof 2025-02-24, the day before the trigger; q62 CAT asof 2021-10-27, the day before the trigger) show the member's own chart; the falling line is not drawn on it, so the keys rest on the 200-day, which the chart shows, and on the dossier's reads (d06, d07, d08, d17, d18). q61's stock closes above its 200-day by the scan's rule (d08); q62's closes 4.9% under it (d17).
